If your intention on the flop was to "call no matter what," then you should shove since you're first to act. Why shove? Because the pot and your stack size don't give you the option of doing much else. By shoving first on the flop, you'll get hands with equity to fold or force them to draw against you at the best possible odds for your situation. Given the action preflop, it really doesn't matter if you had a strong hand or a medium hand; they're both only a pair now and will be played the same way in this situation.

Why isn't check/call a valid option on the flop? Given the read on the table, i.e., passive, anyone willing to bet into you is likely to have a better hand. When a passive player gets aggressive, you should take note and think carefully about what's going on. Check/call is also incorrect because, as mentioned above, shove is better, even though they accomplish the same thing, i.e., getting your stack in. One keeps you in control and tells the aggressive story you're trying to convey with your preflop raise.

It is preferred to open shove here over check/call pretty much always. Again, see points above about each.

You are pot committed on the turn, easily. Many players, myself included, would say you are pot committed on the flop (before you even bet, hence why I argue for a shove). You want to give your opponents the worst odds possible in order to maximize your value.
